Recommended Ranges

The Institute of Medicine guidelines, which ACOG uses, set total gain by pre-pregnancy BMI for a single baby:

Pre-pregnancy BMITotal gainWeekly gain (2nd and 3rd trimesters)
Under 18.528 to 40 lbabout 1 to 1.3 lb
18.5 to 24.925 to 35 lbabout 0.8 to 1 lb
25 to 29.915 to 25 lbabout 0.5 to 0.7 lb
30 or higher11 to 20 lbabout 0.4 to 0.6 lb

Total gain is about 1 to 4.5 lb in the first trimester for most people.

Using the Numbers

  • Ranges are guidelines. Your provider may set a different goal for you.
  • Twin pregnancies have higher ranges; for normal-weight women the IOM range is 37 to 54 lb.
  • Eating for two does not mean double the calories; extra needs are modest and begin in the second trimester.

Check your starting BMI with the BMI calculator.

extra_faqs.q: How much weight should I gain in pregnancy?
extra_faqs.a: It depends on pre-pregnancy BMI. For a normal-weight person with one baby, the guideline is 25 to 35 pounds.
It includes the baby, placenta, amniotic fluid, larger breasts and uterus, extra blood and fluid, and fat stores.

extra_faqs.q: What if I gain too much or too little?
extra_faqs.a: Talk to your provider. They can look at your health, your baby's growth and your nutrition rather than relying on the number alone.
